subject.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads

question: Is retaining only the latest quarantine archive acceptable when repeated overflows replace earlier archived quarantined entries?
rationale: The one-archive policy prevents disk growth but changes how much quarantined state remains recoverable, and repository policy treats persistent-state and fallback behavior as an explicit owner decision.

options.title: Accept latest archive only
options.body: Treat the fixed archive as a bounded diagnostic backup and document or prove that older quarantined entries are not a supported recovery contract.

options.title: Preserve bounded recovery history
options.body: Keep a small bounded archive set or move recoverable quarantine records into the owned SQLite migration and doctor path before merging.

options.title: Keep fail-closed writes
options.body: Avoid rotation and continue rejecting over-cap writes until a durable SQLite-owned quarantine design is available.

recommendation.title: Accept latest archive only
recommendation.body: Treat the fixed archive as a bounded diagnostic backup and document or prove that older quarantined entries are not a supported recovery contract.

likelyOwner.reason: GitHub routed the cron storage review to this likely owner, and the unresolved choice concerns persistence and recovery semantics rather than a mechanical test fix.
